title: scdlbot
description: scdlbot's metrics: downloads, sites, errors, queue, routes, users and resources (https://github.com/gpchelkin/scdlbot).

panels.title: Now (the counts are for the dashboard's time range, like /stats for 24 hours)
Active users
panels.description: Distinct users who sent links or commands in the current UTC day, the last 7 and 30 days (from the bot's database, updated every 5 minutes).

panels.title: Links
panels.description: Download jobs finished in the time range, whatever their result.

panels.title: Done
panels.description: Share of jobs that sent everything. About 9% of SoundCloud tracks are DRM-protected and always fail, so ~90% is normal.

panels.title: Files sent
panels.description: Audios, videos, photos and texts sent (a playlist sends many).

panels.title: Sent to Telegram
panels.description: Bytes uploaded to Telegram.

panels.title: Waiting
panels.description: Jobs waiting in the queues right now.

panels.title: Busy
panels.description: Workers running a job right now, all pools.

panels.title: Up for
panels.description: Time since the bot (re)started. Restarts show as orange marks on the graphs.

panels.title: Jobs by result
panels.description: Finished download jobs per minute, by result.

panels.title: Files sent by kind
panels.description: Files sent per minute. short = YouTube Shorts.

panels.title: Jobs by site
panels.description: Finished jobs per minute by site. other = sites outside the bot's list (Unknown sites setting).

panels.title: Upload to Telegram
panels.description: Upload rate by kind of file.

panels.title: Sites
panels.description: Jobs per site in the time range (like Top sites in /stats). Failed includes timeouts; partial (some playlist items failed) is in neither.

panels.title: Errors by site
panels.description: Download errors in the time range by site and error code. drm: SoundCloud's protected tracks, yt-dlp can't download them.

panels.title: Download errors
panels.description: Failed jobs per minute by error code (the bot's classification of yt-dlp's errors).

panels.title: Telegram errors and rejected links
panels.description: Errors from Telegram while sending, and links refused because of the queue and per-user limits. Empty is good.

panels.title: Video re-encodes
panels.description: Videos re-encoded to h264 (Telegram for iOS plays neither VP9 nor some HEVC), by source codec and result.

panels.title: Queue and workers
panels.description: Jobs waiting and workers busy in each pool (youtube has its own, smaller pool).

panels.title: Wait in queue
panels.description: How long jobs wait before a worker takes them.

panels.title: Job duration
panels.description: Time from a worker taking a job to its last file sent, by kind.

panels.title: Routes in use
panels.description: Red: the route is left out for the site after too many errors, until it recovers.

panels.title: Attempts that worked
panels.description: Share of download attempts that worked, by route. Content errors (DRM, unavailable…) count as failures on every route alike, so compare the routes with each other.

panels.title: Failed attempts by route
panels.description: Failed download attempts per minute by route, without drm (the same on every route). The errors are in Errors by site and Download errors.

panels.title: Tried again elsewhere
panels.description: Downloads tried again through another route after failing through this one, by the error that made it try again.

panels.title: Active users
panels.description: Distinct users in the current UTC day (resets at midnight), the last 7 and 30 days.

panels.title: Telegram app languages, 30 days
panels.description: Share of the last 30 days' users by the language of their Telegram app (Telegram doesn't tell bots users' countries).

panels.title: Messages and buttons
panels.description: Handled updates per minute: *_msg are messages with links in each mode, dl_cmd is /dl, ask_* are the ask buttons, settings_* the settings buttons.

panels.title: Resources (cAdvisor and node_exporter on the same host)
CPU
panels.description: CPU of the services, downloads included (cores), and the bot's CPUQuota.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Memory of the services, downloads included, and the bot's MemoryMax.

panels.title: Downloads killed for memory, restarts
panels.description: OOM kills in the bot's service (downloads are killed first, the bot keeps running) and restarts of the bot. Empty is good.

panels.title: Bot process
panels.description: The bot's main process alone (without downloads): memory and CPU.

panels.title: Disk space free
panels.description: Free space of the host's file systems (DL_DIR holds files being downloaded and sent).
